headlines.title: Uber’s Woes Continue But This Wall Street Pro Says It’s Going to Double WIthin a Year
headlines.summary: Uber sits 30% below its 52-week high while robotaxi fears and weak guidance batter the stock, but one Wall Street analyst just planted a flag that stands far above where even the bulls are willing to go.

headlines.title: Is Uber Stock Worth More Than Its Competitors?
headlines.summary: Uber Technologies (UBER) retains a larger share of its sales as operating profit than four rivals in the ride-hailing, delivery and freight sectors. Investors, however, pay less for each dollar of Uber's earnings than they do for three of those peers. Part of that gap comes from gains outside Uber's operations, which lift its net profit. Even so, the pricing suggests the market doubts the advantage will last.

headlines.title: Is this the best time for investors to buy in on the AI trade?
headlines.summary: Market Hang's panel debates whether it's the best time for investors to get in on the AI trade before chipmaker stocks potentially take off. Today's Market Hang panel consists of Gerber Kawasaki Wealth & Investment Management CEO Ross Gerber, Yahoo Finance's Julie Hyman, Business Insider Today executive editor Dan DeFrancesco, Baird investment strategist Ross Mayfield, and SlateStone Wealth partner and chief market strategist Kenny Polcari.

headlines.title: Uber (UBER) Stock Looks Undervalued With Earnings Priced Below Peers
headlines.summary: Uber Technologies stock has delivered a mixed ride for shareholders, with a strong three year gain sitting alongside weaker shorter term returns. This puts fresh focus on whether its current earnings really support today’s price around US$71. Uber is also leaning hard into autonomous vehicles and new services, which could reshape its profit profile and raises a clear question about what investors are paying for right now. headlines.title: Coupang vs. Uber Technologies: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
headlines.summary: Coupang dominates South Korea with a 0.6% net margin, while Uber scales globally with a 19.3% net margin, a stark contrast in profitability that reshapes the growth narrative.

description: Uber Technologies, Inc. develops and operates proprietary technology applications in the United States, Canada, Latin America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Asia Pacific. The company operates through three segments: Mobility, Delivery, and Freight. The Mobility segment connects consumers with a range of transportation modalities, such as ridesharing, carsharing, micromobility, rentals, public transit, taxis, and other modalities; and offers riders in a variety of vehicle types, as well as financial partnerships products and advertising services. The Delivery segment allows consumers to search for and discover restaurants to grocery, alcohol, convenience, and other retailers, as well as order a meal or other items, and either pick-up at the restaurant or have it delivered; and provides Uber direct, a white-label delivery-as-a-service for retailers and restaurants, as well as advertising services. The Freight segment manages transportation and logistics networks, which connects shippers and carriers in digital marketplace, including carriers upfronts, pricing, and shipment booking; and offers on-demand platform to automate logistics end-to-end transactions for small-and medium-sized businesses to global enterprises. Uber Technologies, Inc. has staetegic partnership with Mews to embed ride booking, real-time tracking and integrated billing directly into the Mews platform. The company was formerly known as Ubercab, Inc. and changed its name to Uber Technologies, Inc. in February 2011. Uber Technologies, Inc. was founded in 2009 and is headquartered in San Francisco, California.
